title: opportunistic-surge-buffer-and-fair-drain-policy
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add an opportunistic per-node surge buffer and proportional tenant drain policy to reduce cross-tenant eviction storms and improve throughput SLO stability under transient spikes. Ship behind feature flag; telemetry and rollout guidance included.
description: Context: transient microbursts from a small set of tenants can trigger aggressive drains and cross-tenant evictions that degrade overall fleet throughput and increase tail latency. Motivation: provide a low-risk, opt-in mechanism to absorb short surges without violating longer-term reservation commitments, and to drain tenants proportionally to their recent contribution to surge pressure. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) an opportunistic surge buffer allocated per-node that can absorb ephemeral excess requests using a bounded credit pool with time-decay, and 2) a proportional fair-drain policy that computes per-tenant drain weights from a short-window surge attribution score instead of blunt LRU-style eviction. Design summary: - Surge buffer is implemented as a soft pool backed by reservoir credits; credits are sourced from ephemeral warm pools and can be reclaimed when under sustained load. Credits decay exponentially with configurable half-life to avoid permanent headroom change. - Buffer admission uses a two-stage check: fast-path optimistic admission when KV cache and batching headroom permit; slow path consults ledger to ensure reservation safety. - Fair-drain computes a tenant surge score based on 1-minute and 5-minute excess request percentiles, and assigns drain weight proportional to score normalized by tenant reservation. This reduces single-tenant eviction storms while preserving guaranteed throughput. - Telemetry added: buffer_utilization_gauge{node}, buffer_reclaims_counter, tenant_surge_score_gauge{tenant}, tenant_drain_weight_gauge{tenant}. - Config: new feature flag dedicated.surge_buffer.enabled (off by default), buffer size percentile, decay_half_life, max_reclaim_rate, drain_smoothing_alpha. Checklist: - [x] core allocator + admission logic implemented in pkg/fleetallocator - [x] controller glue in controllers/fleet to reconcile buffer state per-node - [x] telemetry and prometheus metrics + dashboard panels - [x] unit and integration tests for admission and drain weighting - [x] e2e soak on canary cluster with synthetic microburst workload - [x] feature flag gating and runtime knobs - [x] docs and rollout plan in docs/dedicated/ops/surge-buffer.md Testing & validation: ran synthetic spike suite (benchmarks/ephemeral-spike) showing 35% reduction in eviction count and 12% improvement in P99 latency for non-bursty tenants at same aggregate load. Internal canary run on 3 clusters for 72 hours; no reservation violations observed. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in canary clusters for 48h, then staged rollout to 10% production traffic, monitor buffer_utilization and eviction rate, then 50% and full. If eviction rate rises or reservation slippage shown, rollback gate is automatic via runtime guardrails. Related: follows ENG-2381 and ties into reservation-ledger refactor ENG-2405. Migration notes: none required for persisted state; config added to dedicated configmap. Docs: included operational guidance and recommended default parameters for medium and large fleets.
